html:
The Midday Meal Scheme gives a free cooked lunch every school day to children in India's government schools. It became a national programme in 1995 and is the largest school meal scheme in the world, reaching over 100 million children.

The idea started in the south. Tamil Nadu under K. Kamaraj began school lunches in the 1950s, and Chief Minister M. G. Ramachandran widened them in 1982. The national scheme of 1995 at first often handed out dry grain. In 2001 the Supreme Court, hearing a case on the right to food, ordered every state to serve cooked meals.

Studies found it drew more children, especially girls, into school and kept them there, and helped against hunger. It also brought children of different castes to eat together. Failures have been serious: in 2013 in Bihar, 23 children died after eating a meal cooked with oil stored in a pesticide container. In 2021 it was renamed PM POSHAN. It forms part of a long effort against hunger that runs back to the Green Revolution.
sum: The Midday Meal Scheme gives a free cooked lunch every school day to children in India's government schools. It became a national programme in 1995 and is the largest school meal scheme in the world, reaching over 100 million children.
